# wsgnstat

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mtloots/wsgnstat/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mtloots/wsgnstat/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/wsgnstat)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=wsgnstat)
<!-- badges: end -->

The **two-piece exponential power distribution** on the line and its **wrapped version on the
circle**, treated as a uniform scale mixture with generalised gamma mixing. The package name keeps
the authors' earlier one, the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution. It provides density,
distribution and quantile functions and random generation, the characteristic function and the
trigonometric moments for every shape parameter, and maximum likelihood fitting of the
four-parameter wrapped distribution under a lower bound on the shape, or by the grouped likelihood
for rounded data. The computation runs on a pure-C back-end shared with the Python package of the
same name.

## Installation

From CRAN:

```r
install.packages("wsgnstat")
```

The development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mtloots/wsgnstat", subdir = "wsgnstat")
```

## Example

Simulate from a skew member of the four-parameter wrapped distribution, fit it by maximum
likelihood, and compare with the truth; at a fitted shape above one the standard errors come from
the expected Fisher information:

```{r example}
library(wsgnstat)
set.seed(1)
theta <- rwsgn(200, mu = 1, beta = 1.6, lam = 0.3, sigma = 0.4)
fit <- fit_wsgn(theta)
round(rbind(truth = c(1, 0.4, 0.3, 1.6), estimate = coef(fit), se = fit$se), 3)
```

The characteristic function is computed for every shape, so it equals one at zero also for small
shapes, and at shape 2 with `lam = 0.5` it is the normal characteristic function
`exp(-sigma^2 t^2)`:

```{r anchor}
sapply(c(0.1, 0.3, 1, 2), function(b) Mod(cfsgn(0, 0, 0.4, b, 0.3, 0.7) - 1))
t <- 1:4
rbind(engine = Re(cfsgn(t, 0, 0.4, 2, 0.5, 0.5)), closed_form = exp(-0.16 * t^2))
```

Rounded data are fitted by the grouped likelihood over the recording cells; here the directions
are recorded to 10 degrees:

```{r grouped}
h <- pi / 18
theta10 <- (round(theta / h) * h) %% (2 * pi)
coef(fit_wsgn(theta10, resolution = h, se = "none"))
```

The vignette, `vignette("wsgnstat")`, treats the mixture representation, the characteristic
function for small and large shapes, the accuracy of the wrapped density, the fit with its shape
floor on wind directions, and the grouped likelihood for rounded ant directions.
